claims.text: OpenAI introduced the Codex app on 2026-02-02 as a workspace for managing multiple coding agents and long-running parallel work.
OpenAI introduced GPT-5.3-Codex on 2026-02-05 for coding plus longer-running research, tool use, and complex execution tasks.
The GPT-5.3-Codex System Card was published on 2026-02-05 and applies OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework cybersecurity evaluation to the model.
OpenAI introduced GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark on 2026-02-12 as a research-preview model designed for realtime coding interaction.
Claims such as GPT-5.3-Codex being 25% faster and Codex-Spark exceeding 1,000 tokens/s on Cerebras hardware are vendor-reported performance claims.

limitations.text: The Evidence task intentionally groups four related first-party items; drafting must keep product, base model, system-card, and specialized Spark boundaries explicit.
Performance and benchmark comparisons are vendor-reported.
Codex-Spark’s throughput statement depends on specialized Cerebras hardware and research-preview conditions.
Cyber capability classification must reproduce the System Card’s stated threshold/precaution boundary rather than exaggerating it.
